name: service-events
title: Events
description: Cookieless analytics and transactional server audit events built on OTLP, with inherited actor context, trusted geography and event-derived visits.
docs:
## Overview

Events provides cookieless browser analytics and transactional server recording over the OTLP/HTTP JSON logs endpoint at `/api/otel/v1/logs`. BrowserEvents depends on BrowserOtlp for export; Events depends on Otlp for server telemetry configuration and Effect Crypto for cryptographic operations. Neither feature layer constructs its telemetry foundation. The Events registry item also includes AuditLogTable for in-app organization audit history.

## Storage

### OTLP by default

Browser events are enriched and forwarded to your configured collector. Your telemetry backend owns storage, querying and retention; no application database is required. Forwarding is best effort, not a durable audit archive.

### Optional SQL

Provide a PostgreSQL or SQLite `SqlClient` when you need:

- In-app reports and activity views.
- Shared browser/server visit timelines.
- Audit records committed with business changes.
- Application-owned permissions, backups and retention.

| Table | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `events` | Event data, indexed identity/time fields, optional visit IDs and full OTLP `payload_json` |
| `events_migrations` | Applied schema migration history; no application events |

PostgreSQL uses JSONB with a GIN `jsonb_path_ops` index; SQLite uses JSON text. Visits are derived from event history, without a separate sessions table.

### Delivery

| Path | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Browser, OTLP only | Enrich and forward; no local history or automatic visit IDs |
| Browser, SQL enabled | Write SQL, then forward through OTLP |
| `Otlp.event` | Send server telemetry; no SQL required |
| `Events.track` | Write SQL only; joins transactions using the same SqlClient |

SQL is authoritative: database failure fails ingestion. Committed application-only batches succeed even if forwarding fails; mixed batches retain generic delivery semantics. Browser analytics and generic events can share a batch. Server records are not automatically exported; optionally emit `Otlp.event` after commit. There is no outbox or guaranteed collector delivery.

## Setup

### Install

```bash
bunx shadcn@latest add @krak-stack/service-events
```

Package consumers use `@krak-stack/registry/events`, `/events/browser`, `/events/migrations`, `/events/client`, `/events/schema` and `/events/record`; Otlp is imported from `/opentelemetry`. Server entry points do not import the audit table.

### Server

Enable OTLP logs export, provide Otlp and a platform Crypto layer to Events, then connect ingestion to the HTTP routes. This example uses the Web Crypto-backed layer, which also works in Bun and modern Node:

```ts
import { Layer } from 'effect';
import { BrowserCrypto } from '@effect/platform-browser';
import { Events } from '@/services/events';
import { Otlp } from '@/services/opentelemetry';
import { HttpApiOtlp } from '@/services/opentelemetry/api';

const application = Events.layer.pipe(
  Layer.provide(BrowserCrypto.layer),
  Layer.provideMerge(Otlp.layer),
);
const server = HttpApiOtlp.layer.pipe(
  Layer.provide(Events.ingestionLayer),
  Layer.provideMerge(application),
);
```

`Events.layer` reads the server-only `APP_SECRET` and the origin of `VITE_SITE_URL`. `Events.layerWith(options)` accepts partial overrides; for example, `Events.layerWith({ geolocation: 'cloudflare' })` retains both configuration defaults. Explicit origin or secret values skip their corresponding environment lookup, so fully explicit configuration needs neither variable. Missing or invalid required configuration fails layer acquisition. Geolocation is disabled by default. Provide the Crypto implementation at the application composition root.

`Events.ingestionLayer` connects incoming browser application events to Events for validation, enrichment and optional persistence. Omit it for a plain OTLP proxy. Workers can use application without HTTP routes. The secret must be stable, at least 32 characters and shared across instances. `origin` is a browser allowlist, not authentication.

### Enable SQL

Replace the application layer above with:

```ts
import { Config } from 'effect';
import { PgClient } from '@effect/sql-pg';

const sqlLayer = PgClient.layerConfig({ url: Config.Redacted('DATABASE_URL') });
const application = Events.layer.pipe(
  Layer.provide(sqlLayer),
  Layer.provide(BrowserCrypto.layer),
  Layer.provideMerge(Otlp.layer),
);
```

PgClient provides generic SqlClient; SQLite client layers work too. Provide SQL to Events, not as a sibling layer. Storage mode is fixed at startup; unsupported dialects fail acquisition. `Events.layer` and `Events.layerWith(options)` run migrations; `Events.baseLayer` and `Events.baseLayerWith(options)` leave them to the application. Both With factories accept partial overrides with the same configuration fallbacks. Retain sqlLayer with provideMerge when other application services need the same client for transactions.

### Browser

Mount the composed layer in the browser runtime:

```ts
import { BrowserEvents } from '@/services/events/browser';
import { BrowserOtlp } from '@/services/opentelemetry/browser';

const telemetry = BrowserOtlp.layer({ serviceName: 'my-app-web' });
const browser = BrowserEvents.layer({ locale: () => 'en' }).pipe(
  Layer.provideMerge(telemetry),
);
```

BrowserOtlp owns transport, resources, batching and flushing. Its event exporter is enabled by default; `events: false` disables all event export. BrowserEvents owns page tracking and analytics privacy.

### Service scope and identity

The server service name resolves from Events' `serviceName` override, otherwise Otlp's resource configuration (`OTEL_SERVICE_NAME`, then `service.name` in `OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES`). It scopes visitor hashing, visit lookup and SQL `service_name`; browser names cannot override it. Use distinct names per environment.

With KrakStack Auth, provide `AuthMiddleware.routerLayer({ paths: ['/api/otel/v1/logs'] })` to the telemetry route layer. Verified request `user.id`/`organization.id` annotations replace fallback identity as a whole; ActorRequired owns authorization. Other integrations can supply `identity(request)`, returning verified userId/organizationId or null. Browser identity claims are discarded. Missing identity means anonymous; failed resolution or invalid annotations return 503 rather than silently becoming anonymous.

### Geolocation

| `geolocation` | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Omitted | No IP/geography lookup or automatic visitor/visit attribution |
| `'cloudflare'` | Validated ingress headers; requires origin-bypass protection |
| Effect callback | Trusted application lookup returning optional fields or null; no fallback |

Custom providers return optional `ip` (numeric IPv4/IPv6), `country` (uppercase two-letter code), `region` (subdivision suffix, such as ON) and `city` (nonempty, up to 128 characters). Return only IP for visitors without geography, only geography to omit visitors, or null for neither. Raw IP is used for daily hashing, never stored automatically. Lookup runs per browser batch or request-scoped track call. Invalid results/provider failures fail ingestion (503) or server recording.

## Usage

### Browser tracking

`track` and `page` return Effects. Run them in the mounted browser runtime:

```ts
const orderCompleted = BrowserEvents.track(
  'Order Completed',
  { total: 42 },
  { messageId: 'order-42-completed' },
);
const pageView = BrowserEvents.page({ path: '/orders', name: 'Orders' });
```

| Option | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Event options | Optional messageId, timestamp and context; no client identity |
| `pageViews: false` | Manual integration; initial/SPA pathname views are automatic otherwise |
| `enabled: false` | Disable application analytics, independently of Web Vitals and generic telemetry |
| `respectDoNotTrack` | true; DNT/GPC gate application analytics |
| `sanitizePath` | Replace personal path identifiers with route templates |

Properties become `app.*` attributes. Browser events use no cookies or identity storage and remain analytics; client identity, authentication and audit claims are discarded. Batching is shared with generic events: BrowserOtlp defaults to 30 seconds and 100 records. Configure `events: { exportInterval: '5 seconds', maxBatchSize: 20 }` on BrowserOtlp for faster delivery.

### Server telemetry

Use `Otlp.event` for collector-bound telemetry without SQL:

```ts
const orderCompleted = Otlp.event('order.completed', { total: 42 });
```

### Server recording and audit (SQL)

`Events.track` requires name, accepts optional eventId/category/properties/identity/timestamp, and returns `{ eventId, inserted }`. Category defaults to analytics; omitting eventId generates a fresh UUIDv7 per call through Effect Crypto. Audit events require a typed target with nonempty id, name and type.

```ts
const program = Effect.gen(function* () {
  const events = yield* Events;
  const sql = yield* SqlClient.SqlClient;
  return yield* events.track({
    eventId: `document:${requestId}:deleted`,
    name: 'document.deleted',
    category: 'audit',
    target: { id: documentId, name: documentName, type: 'document' },
  }).pipe(sql.withTransaction);
});
```

Audit requires verified `app.actor.type/id` server annotations, normally supplied by auth. The typed target is stored as `app.audit.target.id/name/type`; it takes precedence over properties and surrounding annotations. Auth supplies standard `user.id` and `user.roles`. Names/photos are not emitted to logs or spans; recorded events retain actor IDs and roles at the time of authorization. Resolve current profiles by actor ID within the organization when displaying the log; show a former-member fallback when membership no longer exists. `user.name` denotes login/username, not display name. Organization API keys do not impersonate human members. A key, session or user-agent header does not prove whether a human, agent, MCP client or CLI initiated the action. Validate domain properties with Effect schemas. Target names and historical roles may contain personal data: record only safe-to-persist values and apply appropriate access and retention policies.

Trusted annotations override derived request context and replace explicit identity as a whole; explicit category wins over annotations/properties. HttpServerRequest enables visitor, visit, geography and device resolution. Background jobs need explicit attribution; untrusted session headers cannot select a visit. Backend requests identify the calling backend, not its users.

Browser DNT/GPC does not disable explicit server recording; apply server opt-out policy yourself. Failed/denied attempts need a transaction that commits. Audit classification does not provide stronger durability, immutable storage or compliance guarantees.

### Audit attribution vocabulary

Actor identifies whose authority the operation used; Method identifies how the request authenticated. Store both in the unchanged OTLP EventLogRecord, without attempting to reconstruct the execution path.

| Concern | Attributes | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Responsible principal | `app.actor.type`, `app.actor.id` | Auth emits user/user ID or organization/organization ID. A key is a credential, not the actor. Background services may explicitly identify a system principal. |
| Request authentication | `app.auth.method` | `session` or `api_key`, recorded by verified auth. This is not the original login provider or proof of human interaction. |
| Credential | `app.auth.credential.id` | API-key record ID; never the secret or a session token. User and organization keys retain their key identity here. |
| User and historical roles | `user.id`, `user.roles` | Verified user and organization roles at authorization time, when a user exists. |
| Organization scope | `organization.id` | Custom application organization scope; distinct from the responsible principal. |
| Business target | `app.audit.target.id/name/type` | Target identity and safe name snapshot from the typed audit payload. |

This is an application audit vocabulary using OTLP, not a claim of OTel audit-schema or OCSF conformance. Use official [OTel user attributes](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/registry/attributes/user/) where applicable. Relevant GenAI/MCP attributes such as `gen_ai.agent.id` and `mcp.method.name` can remain in explicitly instrumented telemetry as context; the audit table does not interpret them as Method. There is no custom executor/channel contract. The [OCSF Actor object](https://schema.ocsf.io/objects/actor) and [API Activity](https://schema.ocsf.io/classes/api_activity) provide richer security-event models; exporting OCSF requires a deliberate mapping to its full event schema.

Examples: a signed-in request has actor user/user ID and auth method session; a user key has the same user principal plus auth method api_key and credential ID; an organization key has an organization principal with no invented human identity. A key identifies its owning principal, not necessarily its physical operator. Missing authentication metadata stays absent rather than being stored as manual or unknown.

### Audit queries and table (SQL)

The Events install includes both `Events.listAudit` and `AuditLogTable`; no separate audit service or flattened entry schema is needed. Authorize organization access in the application before querying.

```ts
const events = yield* Events;
const page = yield* events.listAudit({
  organizationId, page: 0, pageSize: 20,
  globalFilter: 'document',
  sort: [{ id: 'time', direction: 'desc' }],
});
```

`listAudit` uses the shared Query schema and returns `{ data, meta }`: unchanged EventLogRecord values plus page, pageSize, total and pageCount. SQL persistence is required. Queries are restricted to the configured server service and requested organization, excluding browser and non-audit events.

Supported sort IDs are `time`, `eventName`, `recordType`, `record`, `actorType` and `actorId`; default order is newest first with an event-ID tie breaker. Search matches event names, target IDs/names/types, actor IDs/types and member IDs, not current profiles. Actor and Method column sorting are disabled.

```tsx
import { AuditLogTable } from '@/services/events/client/audit-log-table';

<AuditLogTable
  entries={page.data}
  rowCount={page.meta.total}
  state={query}
  onStateChange={setQuery}
  actors={[
    { type: "organization", id: organization.id, label: organization.name, imageSrc: organization.logo },
    ...members.map((member) => ({
      type: "user" as const,
      id: member.userId,
      label: member.user.name,
      description: member.user.email,
      imageSrc: member.user.image,
    })),
  ]}
/>
```

The five columns are Time, Action, Target, Actor and Method. Actor resolves the responsible user or organization. Method reads only `app.auth.method`: session displays User session, api_key displays API Key, and missing or unsupported values display Unknown. It does not infer Manual, Agent, MCP or CLI labels from other telemetry.

Package imports are `@krak-stack/registry/events/client` and `/events/record`. Paging, filtering and sorting live in the standard Query state; rowCount supplies only the total matching records. Locale defaults to KrakstackProvider, with an optional `locale` override for labels, dates and table controls. English and French defaults are included. Member images use the reference cell's default circle style.

`actors` contains current profiles the viewer may access, each with `{ type: "user" | "organization", id, label, description?, imageSrc? }`. The table matches both type and ID, including user impersonators. Fetch organization-scoped profiles on the client and normalize auth asset URLs before passing them in; never enrich persisted logs with profile data. Missing users display Member with their actor ID; missing organizations display Organization with their actor ID. These neutral labels also cover loading, partial lists and unavailable profiles, without incorrectly identifying a former member. Unresolved impersonators retain their recorded ID. Other principals retain their recorded type and ID. Historical roles come from the log's `user.roles`, not current membership. Use `renderAction` for domain-specific labels, `messages` for locale-keyed label overrides, and `loading` or `error` for query status.

### IDs and retries

SQL deduplicates by `(service_name, source, event_id)`, separating browser and server IDs. Supply a stable eventId for retryable server operations. A generated ID does not deduplicate separate calls.

- Same ID and content: retain the original record; return inserted:false.
- Same ID, different caller-owned content: EventConflictError; browser batches return 409 and roll back.
- Different IDs: separate events, even with matching content.

### Visit timelines (SQL)

Automatic visits require SQL and trusted IP/User-Agent. Browser and request-scoped server events share a visit when service, secret, IP and User-Agent match. Daily visitor IDs are approximate pseudonymous SHA-256 hashes with a server-only salt derived from the secret, service and UTC day. The v2 derivation changes IDs from the previous HMAC algorithm.

| Rule | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Receipt inactivity under 30 minutes | Reuse visit; otherwise new UUIDv7 |
| Retry | Original record/visit; does not extend activity |
| Midnight UTC | Daily visitor rotation splits new visits, not retries |
| Missing IP/User-Agent | No automatic attribution for new events |

Group/filter SQL `session_id` (OTLP `session.id`) for timelines; order by occurred_at/event_id. PostgreSQL advisory locks or SQLite writer locks serialize lookup and insertion. Retain at least 30 minutes of history; cleanup is application-owned. Session IDs are grouping keys, not access tokens: scope every query by service and verified organization/user.

### Web Vitals

Browser Web Vitals is included in [OpenTelemetry](./service-opentelemetry). Enable its opt-in layer alongside BrowserEvents:

```ts
import { BrowserWebVitals } from '@/services/opentelemetry/web-vitals';

const browser = Layer.mergeAll(
  BrowserEvents.layer(),
  BrowserWebVitals.layer(),
).pipe(Layer.provideMerge(telemetry));
```

Web Vitals have their own DNT/GPC policy, independent of application analytics' enabled setting. The shared exporter preserves `krakstack.events` for generic telemetry and `krakstack.application.events` for analytics, so Web Vitals are not stored in SQL. Base browser entry points do not import web-vitals.

### Operational boundaries

Own permissions, backups, retention and reporting UI. Apply edge rate limits/bot filtering and keep IDs out of metric/Loki labels.

| Boundary | Policy |
| --- | --- |
| Scope | krakstack.application.events; app.event.schema.version=1; generic telemetry uses krakstack.events |
| Browser context | analytics.* attributes; producer resource preserved |
| Audit fields | app.actor.*, app.auth.*, app.audit.*, app.event.* and organization.id are custom conventions, not OTel audit standards |
| Requests | JSON, 64 KiB, at most 100 application records, matching Origin |
| Timestamps | Previous hour through one minute ahead |
| Privacy | No automatic raw IP/UA, full URLs, titles or ad IDs; properties are caller-owned |
